# Which harness should I use?

<!-- Generated by scripts/scoreboard/build.ts from docs/scoreboard/entries/*.json and the results files they name. Do not edit by hand. -->

One table per task set. **Never compare numbers across tables:** different tasks give different pass rates. Every number below is read from a committed results file; the receipts line under each table names the files.

## 20 public v0.3 multi-user dev tasks (matrix-mu-2026-11, dev, public)

**Saturated task set.** On these tasks pass rate can't separate the harnesses: 14 of 20 tasks scored the same in every cell, and a gap smaller than 7.7 to 14.2 points (alpha 0.05; 9.5 to 17.6 at the first Holm step) is unlikely to show. Cost per solved task and median time per trial do differ between harnesses (descriptive, no test).

- **Opus 5.5:** 3 preregistered pairs: 3 can't tell apart.
- **GPT-6.1 Sol:** 3 preregistered pairs: 3 can't tell apart.

**Caveats:**

- Dev tasks at these pins: a result here is not a held-out confirmation.
- Claude Code and Codex are each model's own harness; they can't run the same model, so they are never compared with each other.
- Every cell is a plain harness: no gstack, no gbrain.
- Cost per solved task is the cell's whole spend at list price through our metering proxy, divided by its scored passes; spend includes excluded trials.
- Time is the median wall-clock time per trial, one trial at a time on one VM per cell.
- Calls come only from the run's preregistered comparisons; rows are in the run's own order, which is not a ranking.
- OpenClaw, Opus 5.5: Incomplete cell: the last task's final reps ended in a cap stop, so scored trials are fewer than planned.
- OpenClaw, Opus 5.5: Lists Haiku as its housekeeping model (shipped default); it made no housekeeping calls.
- QM (Pi loop), Opus 5.5: Ran on the default Docker bridge, so the network was not held fixed and QM's comparisons are secondary and untested.
- QM (Pi loop), Opus 5.5: Uses Haiku for housekeeping (shipped default, metered inside its cost).
- OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol: Incomplete cell: every rep of the last task ended in a cap stop, so that task drops from its comparisons.
- OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol: Cost per solved task is the headline figure; its interval uses each trial record's own cost, which leaves out one timed-out charge logged after its trial closed.
- Why null? verdict: **FIX-METHOD**. See [the glossary below](#how-to-read-this) and the report.

## How to read this

- **Pass rate:** each task's share of passing scored tries, averaged over the tasks.
- **95% range:** the task-clustered bootstrap interval: tasks are resampled with replacement, so a few lucky tasks can't narrow it.
- **Can't tell apart:** the run's preregistered test, adjusted for the number of comparisons (Holm), found no difference. It does not mean equal: a gap smaller than the stated detectable difference is unlikely to show.
- **Interval only, not tested:** the run reports a range for this pair but its preregistration made no test of it.
- **Cost per solved task:** what the cell spent at list price, metered by our proxy, divided by its passes. **Cost per trial** is the same spend divided by the trials recorded.
- **Median time per trial:** wall-clock time from start to finish of one trial.
- **Saturated task set:** half or more of the tasks scored the same in every cell, so the tasks, not the harness, decide most of the score.
- **KEEP:** tested on frontier models and it helps, or it is needed; keep it on. **FIX-METHOD:** the test could not tell, for a named reason; fix the test before deciding. **CUT-CANDIDATE:** tested fairly and it did not help; a candidate to switch off.
